main_text.p: 2. MATERIAM pituitosam per carnem & habitum corporis totum sparsam, primum apparatibus dictis in ascite: ut, mel le rosato, oxymelite simplici, syrup. duarum & quinque radicum, cum aqua absinthij, foeniculi, cassuthae per dies quinque, aut sex: diutius enim apparanda, quam ascitae materia fluxilis et liquida, ventriculo propinqua, & hepati. Deinde vacuantibus: ut, hierae picrae mellitae uncia una, vel eiusdem semuncia cum agarici trochiscati drachma una, vel pilularum de rhabarbaro drac. duabus, quarto quoque die sumptis: (pituitam enim, & ex hac putrefacta bilem purgant, & hepar roborant) vel rhabarbari, & agarici trochiscati, ana scrip. duobus septimo quoque die sumptis, vel diaphoenico, scrup. indo. quamuis scammonium hepati noxium est: post ea autem scammoniata dantur, quae noxam emendent, aut potius cum his vel ante hac, quae noxam prohibeant: in quibus enim affectibus hepar imbecillum est, quae ipsum laedant,

page.notes: Printed text is in italic throughout; the running head is set in roman caps; the page is slightly faded at the top right with show-through from the reverse, which is omitted. Some words are uncertain in the old spelling (e.g. "cassuthae", "scrip.") and are transcribed as printed.
